answer: The network checks location itself. Independent probes on separate continents time round trips to each seat, triangulate its position, and hash the path; a seat is admitted only when that signature is unique in the register. Two seats behind one transit arrangement void each other, so a raven running clones under a single hosting contract loses all of them together, and spreading out means renting separate routes with separate contracts. A distinct path is a fresh, non-transferable expense, like a forge striking each marble from its own die instead of pressing copies from one mold.
